why: cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py::survey_the_corpus resolves the trail TWICE, through two different doors, and only the first one follows the device. Line 143 asks domain.diagnostic_trail() — which honours _diagnostic_roots, so it moves when the device moves — and sets `exists` from it. Line 148 then builds BreadcrumbLog('inference_domain', 0) with NO roots, which re-derives the LIVE ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0 and reads its records. So `trail_exists` describes one directory and `post_era_lines`/`trail_misses` describe another. This is precisely the failure the function's own docstring says it exists to prevent: 'if the device's berth ever moves, a probe carrying its own copy of the address goes on reading an empty directory and reports a catastrophe that is really a stale constant' — and the probe is carrying its own copy on the read half. IT WAS A HOLLOW GREEN, NOT A LATENT ONE. The proof tooth test_the_probe_reads_the_address_the_device_declares asserts trail_misses >= 1 after writing ONE line into an isolated trail. It has been passing on the live trail's historical lines, not on the line it just wrote — the tooth's own subject was never measured. Surfaced 2026-09-08 by ticket 1c4ae8f053fe, which stopped copying the ~/.cairn trail tree into the tester's sandbox: with an empty live logs tree the borrowed lines vanished and the read half returned 0. The seal did not break the proof; it removed the accident the proof was passing on.
